claim: This review is decision-grade only for field taxonomy, emerging variable-impedance method branches and coverage gaps. It reports that linear unknown-coefficient interaction models remain prevalent and that many learning approaches optimize parameters of a linear impedance law rather than learn a nonlinear interaction-port law. Its heterogeneous narrative literature cannot support pooled performance, safety or method-superiority conclusions.
claim_locator: Model taxonomy; linear/nonlinear/fuzzy/fractional/learning comparison; applications; review-method reporting.
problem_and_setting: Surveying variable impedance/admittance for HRI/HRC across simulations, low-DOF systems, exoskeletons, haptics, polishing, teleoperation and pHRI.
method_or_mechanism: Organizes linear versus nonlinear models and catalogs fractional calculus, type-I/II fuzzy systems, sliding mode, neural networks, RL, MPC and iterative learning. Many learning methods tune parameters within linear impedance; nonlinear/fuzzy/fractional variants add expressiveness with computation, tuning, data and interpretability burdens.
content_summary: The 247 references mix reviews, theory, simulations, generic control, non-HRI and pHRI; some are not direct port-impedance evidence. No common benchmark or meta-analysis exists. References include 2025 without a search cutoff. Reported percentage improvements are not comparable or poolable. Safety is typically an intended benefit without synthesized collision, force-limit, clinical or standards outcomes.
synthesis_role: Field taxonomy, emerging-method catalog and coverage-gap evidence only.
development_link: Separates classical linear parameter adaptation from nonlinear port modeling, fuzzy/fractional methods and learning optimization, highlighting benchmark, high-DOF and safety-synthesis gaps.

evidence.finding: Linear unknown-coefficient models remain prevalent for simplicity and interpretability.
Many NN/RL/MPC/iterative methods tune parameters of assumed linear impedance rather than learn nonlinear port laws.
Nonlinear/fuzzy/fractional approaches add capacity but computation, tuning, data and interpretability burdens.
Evidence is concentrated in simulation and low-DOF settings, with sparse high-DOF industrial coverage.
No synthesized collision injury, force-limit, clinical or standards outcomes support broad safety claims.
No databases, search strings/dates, PRISMA flow, eligibility, deduplication, extraction or quality appraisal are documented.
Heterogeneous tasks and outcomes prevent pooling percentages or ranking methods.

boundary_conditions: Use only for taxonomy and gaps.
Do not infer pooled effectiveness or safety.
Simulation/low-DOF evidence does not establish high-DOF performance.
assumptions: The admitted full text is complete.
Labels follow the article even when examples indirectly concern port impedance.
Absent documented procedures are not proof no informal search occurred.

reported: Linear models miss nonlinear human behavior and hysteresis.
inferred: The review is not reproducibly systematic.
General safety or superiority is unsupported.
